name: TA505
summary: TA505 is a cyber criminal group that has been active since at least 2014. TA505 is known for frequently changing malware, driving global trends in criminal malware distribution, and ransomware campaigns involving Clop.

procedures.text: TA505 has registered domains to impersonate services such as Dropbox to distribute malware.
TA505 has used malware such as Azorult and Cobalt Strike in their operations.
TA505 has used a variety of tools in their operations, including AdFind, BloodHound, Mimikatz, and PowerSploit.
TA505 has staged malware on actor-controlled domains.
TA505 has used stolen domain admin accounts to compromise additional hosts.
TA505 has used spearphishing emails with malicious attachments to initially compromise victims.
TA505 has sent spearphishing emails containing malicious links.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a local user account.
TA505 has used PowerShell to download and execute malware and reconnaissance scripts.
TA505 has executed commands using `cmd.exe`.
TA505 has deployed payloads that use Windows API calls on a compromised host.
Dridex: Dridex can maintain persistence via the creation of scheduled tasks within system directories such as `windows\system32\`, `windows\syswow64,` `winnt\system32`, and `winnt\syswow64`.

TA505 has used lures to get users to enable content in malicious attachments and execute malicious files contained in archives. For example, TA505 makes their malware look like legitimate Microsoft Word documents,.pdf and/or.lnk files.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy leverages WMI to enumerate anti-virus on the victim.
TA505 has used VBS for code execution.
TA505 has used JavaScript for code execution.
TA505 has used lures to get users to click links in emails and attachments. For example, TA505 makes their malware look like legitimate Microsoft Word documents,.pdf and/or.lnk files.
TA505 has leveraged malicious Word documents that abused DDE.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use PsExec to execute a payload on a remote host. It can also use Service Control Manager to start new services.
Dridex: Dridex can abuse legitimate Windows executables to side-load malicious DLL files.
Get2: Get2 has the ability to run executables with command-line arguments.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Python to perform execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can download a hosted "beacon" payload using BITSAdmin.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can exploit Oracle Java vulnerabilities for execution, including CVE-2011-3544, CVE-2013-2465, CVE-2012-4681, and CVE-2013-2460.
TrickBot: TrickBot used COM to setup scheduled task for persistence.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit contains a collection of Privesc-PowerUp modules that can discover and exploit path interception opportunities in the PATH environment variable.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit contains a collection of Privesc-PowerUp modules that can discover and exploit search order hijacking vulnerabilities.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit contains a collection of Privesc-PowerUp modules that can discover and exploit unquoted path vulnerabilities.
TA505 has used malware to disable Windows Defender through modification of the Registry.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has established persistence via the `HKCU\SOFTWARE\microsoft\windows\currentversion\run` registry key.
TrickBot: TrickBot establishes persistence by creating an autostart service that allows it to run whenever the machine boots.
ServHelper: ServHelper has added a user named "supportaccount" to the Remote Desktop Users and Administrators groups.
ServHelper: ServHelper has created a new user named "supportaccount".
Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper contains an implementation of an SSP.

Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper has been extended to include Skeleton Key domain controller authentication bypass functionality. The `LSADUMP::ChangeNTLM` and `LSADUMP::SetNTLM` modules can also manipulate the password hash of an account without knowing the clear text value.
Net: The `net user username \password \domain` commands in Net can be used to create a domain account.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to use an Excel Workbook to execute additional code by enabling Office to trust macros and execute code without user permission.
TrickBot: TrickBot can implant malicious code into a compromised device's firmware.
SDBbot: SDBbot has the ability to use application shimming for persistence if it detects it is running as admin on Windows XP or 7, by creating a shim database to patch services.exe.
SDBbot: SDBbot has the ability to use image file execution options for persistence if it detects it is running with admin privileges on a Windows version newer than Windows 7.
TA505 has been seen injecting a DLL into winword.exe.
Azorult: Azorult can decrypt the payload into memory, create a new suspended process of itself, then inject a decrypted payload to the new process and resume new process execution.
TrickBot: TrickBot has used `Nt*` Native API functions to inject code into legitimate processes such as `wermgr.exe`.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can exploit vulnerabilities such as MS14-058.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit's `Invoke-TokenManipulation` Exfiltration module can be used to manipulate tokens.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can steal access tokens from exiting processes.
Azorult: Azorult can call WTSQueryUserToken and CreateProcessAsUser to start a new process with local system privileges.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can make tokens from known credentials.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can spawn processes with alternate PPIDs.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `MISC::AddSid` module can append any SID or user/group account to a user's SID-History. Mimikatz also utilizes SID-History Injection to expand the scope of other components such as generated Kerberos Golden Tickets and DCSync beyond a single domain.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use a number of known techniques to bypass Windows UAC.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `sudo` to run a command.
TA505 has decrypted packed DLLs with an XOR key.
TA505 has leveraged `rundll32.exe` to execute malicious DLLs.
Dridex: Dridex's strings are obfuscated using RC4.
TA505 has used UPX to obscure malicious code.
TA505 has password-protected malicious Word documents.
Azorult: Azorult can delete files from victim machines.
TA505 has used `msiexec` to download and execute malicious Windows Installer files.
TA505 has used base64 encoded PowerShell commands.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike includes a capability to modify the Beacon payload to eliminate known signatures or unpacking methods.
Clop: Clop has used the `sleep` command to avoid sandbox detection.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike's `execute-assembly` command can run a.NET executable within the memory of a sacrificial process by loading the CLR.
TrickBot: The TrickBot downloader has used an icon to appear as a Microsoft Word document.
ServHelper: ServHelper has created a new user named `supportaccount`.
SDBbot: SDBbot has the ability to clean up and remove data structures from a compromised host.
Net: The `net use \\system\share /delete` command can be used in Net to remove an established connection to a network share.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can timestomp any files or payloads placed on a target machine to help them blend in.
Dridex: Dridex can use `regsvr32.exe` to initiate malicious code.
Cobalt Strike: The Cobalt Strike loader can use the `MessageBoxA` API to prompt for user interaction as an anti-sandbox measure.
TrickBot: TrickBot has used a hidden VNC (hVNC) window to monitor the victim and collect information stealthily.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use spoof arguments in spawned processes that execute beacon commands.
TA505 has signed payloads with code signing certificates from Thawte and Sectigo.
TA505 has used malware to disable Windows Defender.
TA505 has used.iso files to deploy malicious.lnk files.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCShadow` module can be used to make AD updates by temporarily setting a computer to be a DC.
TA505 has used malware to gather credentials from Internet Explorer.
TA505 has used malware to gather credentials from FTP clients and Outlook.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from the LSASS Memory.

procedures.text: FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can collect mouse events.
TrickBot: TrickBot has the ability to capture RDP credentials by capturing the `CredEnumerateA` API
TrickBot: TrickBot uses brute-force attack against RDP with rdpscanDll module.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO::Extract` module can extract keys by interacting with Windows cryptographic application programming interface (API) functions.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit contains a collection of Exfiltration modules that can harvest credentials from Group Policy Preferences.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from the credential vault and DPAPI.

procedures.text: TrickBot: TrickBot can steal passwords from the KeePass open source password manager.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create golden tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create silver tickets.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit's `Invoke-Kerberoast` module can request service tickets and return crackable ticket hashes.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO` module can create and export various types of authentication certificates.
Azorult: Azorult can collect the username from the victim’s machine.

Azorult: Azorult can collect the machine information, system architecture, the OS version, computer name, Windows product name, the number of CPU cores, video card information, and the system language.
Clop: Clop can enumerate all processes on the victim's machine.
AdFind: AdFind can extract subnet information from Active Directory.

AdFind: AdFind has the ability to query Active Directory for computers.

procedures.text: FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy enumerates the privilege level of the victim during the initial infection.
AdFind: AdFind can enumerate domain groups.

AdFind: AdFind can enumerate domain users.

AdFind: AdFind can gather information about organizational units (OUs) and domain trusts from Active Directory.

procedures.text: TrickBot: TrickBot collects a list of install programs and services on the system’s machine.
Azorult: Azorult can check for installed software on the system under the Registry key `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall`.
TA505 has used TinyMet to enumerate members of privileged groups. TA505 has also run `net group /domain`.
TA505 has used the tool EmailStealer to steal and send lists of e-mail addresses to a remote server.
Clop: Clop can search for processes with antivirus and antimalware product names.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can produce a sessions report from compromised hosts.
Azorult: Azorult can collect the time zone information from the system.
Dridex: Dridex has collected a list of installed software on the system.
Amadey: Amadey does not run any tasks or install additional malware if the victim machine is based in Russia.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can perform port scans from an infected host.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy will attempt to detect if a usable smart card is current inserted into a card reader.
Net: The `net accounts` and `net accounts /domain` commands with Net can be used to obtain password policy information.

Clop: Clop has checked the keyboard language using the GetKeyboardLayout() function to avoid installation on Russian-language or other Commonwealth of Independent States-language machines; it will also check the `GetTextCharset` function.
BloodHound: BloodHound has the ability to collect local admin information via GPO.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can start a VNC-based remote desktop server and tunnel the connection through the already established C2 channel.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Window admin shares (C$ and ADMIN$) for lateral movement.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `SEKURLSA::Pth` module can impersonate a user, with only a password hash, to execute arbitrary commands.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can deliver Beacon payloads for lateral movement by leveraging remote COM execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can SSH to a remote service.
TrickBot: TrickBot has used a VNC module to monitor the victim and collect information to pivot to valuable systems on the network
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `WinRM` to execute a payload on a remote host.
TrickBot: TrickBot utilizes EternalBlue and EternalRomance exploits for lateral movement in the modules wormwinDll, wormDll, mwormDll, nwormDll, tabDll.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCSync` and `KERBEROS::PTT` modules implement the three steps required to extract the krbtgt account hash and create/use Kerberos tickets.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has collected information and files from a compromised machine.
Azorult: Azorult can capture screenshots of the victim’s machines.
Dridex: Dridex can perform browser attacks via web injects to steal information such as credentials, certificates, and cookies.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can collect clipboard data.
PowerSploit: PowerSploit's `Get-MicrophoneAudio` Exfiltration module can record system microphone audio.
SDBbot: SDBbot has the ability to record video on a compromised host.
BloodHound: BloodHound can compress data collected by its SharpHound ingestor into a ZIP file to be written to disk.
TA505 has used HTTP to communicate with C2 nodes.
TA505 has downloaded additional malware to execute on victim systems.
Azorult: Azorult can encrypt C2 traffic using XOR.
TA505 has used fast flux to mask botnets by distributing payloads across multiple IPs.
Dridex: Dridex has encrypted traffic with RSA.

Dridex: Dridex contains a backconnect module for tunneling network traffic through a victim's computer. Infected computers become part of a P2P botnet that can relay C2 traffic to other infected peers.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can be configured to use TCP, ICMP, and UDP for C2 communications.
TrickBot: TrickBot can Base64-encode C2 commands.
Dridex: Dridex contains a module for VNC.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy may obfuscate portions of the initial C2 handshake.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can leverage the HTTP protocol for C2 communication, while hiding the actual data in either an HTTP header, URI parameter, the transaction body, or appending it to the URI. Cobalt Strike
TrickBot: TrickBot can use secondary C2 servers for communication after establishing connectivity and relaying victim information to primary C2 servers.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can conduct peer-to-peer communication over Windows named pipes encapsulated in the SMB protocol. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use a custom command and control protocol that can be encapsulated in DNS. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can be configured to have commands relayed over a peer-to-peer network of infected hosts. This can be used to limit the number of egress points, or provide access to a host without direct internet access.
TrickBot: TrickBot has been known to reach a command and control server via one of nine proxy IP addresses.
Dridex: Dridex can use multiple layers of proxy servers to hide terminal nodes in its infrastructure.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to accept a value for HTTP Host Header to enable domain fronting.

TrickBot: Some TrickBot samples have used HTTP over ports 447 and 8082 for C2. Newer versions of TrickBot have been known to use a custom communication protocol which sends the data unencrypted over port 443.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike uses a custom command and control protocol that is encapsulated in HTTP, HTTPS, or DNS. In addition, it conducts peer-to-peer communication over Windows named pipes encapsulated in the SMB protocol. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has sent data collected from a compromised host to its C2 servers.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can set its Beacon payload to reach out to the C2 server on an arbitrary and random interval.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike will break large data sets into smaller chunks for exfiltration.
TA505 has used a wide variety of ransomware, such as Clop, Locky, Jaff, Bart, Philadelphia, and GlobeImposter, to encrypt victim files and demand a ransom payment.
Clop: Clop can kill several processes and services related to backups and security solutions.
Clop: Clop can delete the shadow volumes with `vssadmin Delete Shadows /all /quiet` and can use bcdedit to disable recovery options.
TrickBot: TrickBot module "Trickboot" can write or erase the UEFI/BIOS firmware of a compromised device.
